title: He Built a Simple App and Sold It for $200 Million
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast

stated_problem.quote: If you put people in a lobby with three strangers, they're either going to draw anatomical body parts or they're just going to be rude.
stated_problem.speaker: Dan Porter

idea.name: Draw Something
idea.one_liner: A social drawing-and-guessing game for friends, distributed as an iPhone game.
idea.customer: People who want to play a simple, social game with friends.
idea.offer: Players draw prompts for friends to guess, with shared streaks and live drawing playback.

key_quotes.quote: So, when we made it for the phone, we only let you play your friends because we were like, we can't stop people from drawing funny things or being annoying.
And then I was like, Oh, it's like a streak. And then I was like, Oh, a streak is a way that two people can play a game and be on the same team and not be competitive.

claims.claim: The game stayed at number one every day for six months.
claims.quote: It shot to number one and it stayed there every single day for 6 months.

claims.claim: 25 million people played per day.
claims.quote: 25 million people a day were playing it.

claims.claim: It was the number one game in 60 countries.
claims.quote: It's the number one game in 60 countries in the world.

claims.claim: A quarter of a billion people downloaded it.
claims.quote: It's the number one game in 60 countries in the world and a quarter of a billion people downloaded it.

claims.claim: The game sold for $200 million.
claims.quote: And what did you end up selling it for? $200 million.

claims.claim: 80-year-olds played the game.
claims.quote: 80-year-olds played my game. It was so simple.

acquisition_channels.details: Players could invite friends from their contact lists.

ideas.delivery: Dan designed the game with company developers; players used it on iPhones to draw and guess with friends.

idea.name: OMGPOP multiplayer gaming site
idea.one_liner: A multiplayer gaming company and site where people played games together online.
idea.customer: The people who played OMGPOP's games; Dan says they were mostly 14-year-old girls in California.
idea.offer: A gaming site with multiple games that people could play with one another.

key_quotes.quote: So, we changed the name, we understood who the audience was and we started to grow and we added more and more games and built just kind of like a gaming site where people came and played with each other.

claims.claim: The customers were mostly 14-year-old girls in California.
claims.quote: Got deep into Google Analytics and so forth and I realized that the customers were actually almost entirely 14-year-old girls in California.

claims.claim: They played for four or five hours a day.
claims.quote: That's who was playing the games for four or five hours a day.

claims.claim: The company had millions of users.
claims.quote: It was good and then we were successful and we had millions of users.

claims.claim: Average time on site was four and a half to five hours.
claims.quote: Average time on site was four and a half to five hours.

claims.claim: The company had about three million users when FarmVille had 100 million.
claims.quote: All of a sudden, they had 100 million users. We had like 3 million users.

acquisition_channels.details: Dan says a misspelled company name was losing Google traffic; they changed the name and started to grow.

ideas.delivery: The company built and hosted multiplayer games on its gaming site.
